gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's Elite 400 solar input stops at 60 V and 20 A while its 350 W panel is 33 V open-circuit, so the Elite 400 + 2× 350 W kit cannot be wired in series (66 V) and in parallel is capped below 660 W of its 700 W, whereas the 2× 200 W kit fits in series at 49.2 V.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages and one more StormWatts result. PowerSized's DELTA Pro 3 review gives only '2,600 W' solar and no voltage, amps or wiring. StormWatts' 240 V solar-input page does the series/parallel arithmetic for DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus, S5000 and Explorer 5000 Plus only. StormWatts' bundle-vs-separate page has no voltage, amps or connector data. StormWatts' same-panel-watts kit page (not cited) comes closest: it runs the same check for the Elite 200 V2 with two SP200L panels (series about 49 V fits, parallel 21.6 A over 20 A). None of the four mentions the Elite 400, the 350 W panel's 33 V, or the 2× 350 W kit.
decides: Among the 3,840 Wh kits we link, it favours the Elite 400 + 2× 200 W kit ($1,804.05 link price, $1,899 store) over the 2× 350 W kit ($2,325.60 link, $2,448 store): the 200 W pair delivers its full rated 400 W in series inside the 60 V limit, while the 350 W pair cannot reach 700 W into this station. The page's refill-hours column for the 2× 350 W kit should use under 660 W (at least 5.8 h), not 700 W (5.5 h). It does not change the ships-now rule: every Elite 400 kit is a pre-order, and BLUETTI's page today says mid-January for orders from Nov 18. The ships-now pick has to come from elsewhere (ALLPOWERS R3500 kits at 3,168 Wh sit at the edge of the 20% line; I did not research their solar limits).
candidates: Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus + 2× SolarSaga 200 W kit

findings.label: Solar input limit (maker's US page)
findings.note: Page text: 'Solar: 1,000 W Max., 12–60 V, 20 A Max.' The page names no connector type. The same line appears on the 2× 350 W kit page.

findings.label: Station box contents (no solar cable listed)
findings.value: Elite 400 × 1, AC charging cable 1.8 m × 1, grounding screw × 1, user manual × 1
findings.note: The solar cable comes with the panel, not the station (see the 350 W panel row).

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage, connector, included cable
findings.value: 33 V Voc; MC4; one 20 A MC4-to-XT60 solar charging cable (1.5 m) in the box
findings.note: Page text: 'industry-standard MC4 connectors and a 33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)' and '20A MC4 to XT60 Solar Charging Cable (1.5m) x 1'. The Tech Specs table was empty in the fetch, so Isc, Vmp and Imp were not readable. $649 each, $1,298 for two (storecheck, 2026-11-18).

findings.label: Maker's compatibility list includes the Elite 400
findings.value: Listed: AC200P, AC200MAX, AC300, EB150, EB240, EP500, EP500PRO, AC500, Apex 300, Elite 300, Elite 400, AC200L, AC180, Pioneer Na, Elite 100 V2, AC180T, AC70, Elite 200 V2, AC240, AC200P L, Premium 200 V2, AC180P
findings.note: The page gives no series/parallel guidance and states no exclusions.

findings.label: Two 350 W panels in series against the 60 V limit (arithmetic)
findings.value: 2 × 33 V = 66 V open-circuit, 6 V over the 60 V maximum
findings.note: Arithmetic from BLUETTI's own figures: 33 V Voc (350 W panel page) × 2 against 12–60 V (kit page). Voc rises further in cold weather. The kit page gives no wiring guidance and does not list bundle contents or the panel model. Kit store price $2,448.00 (storecheck, 2026-11-18).

findings.label: Two 350 W panels in parallel against the 20 A limit (arithmetic ceiling)
findings.value: under 660 W of the 700 W rated (20 A × 33 V); refill at that ceiling 3,840 Wh / 660 W = at least 5.8 h, against 5.5 h at 700 W
findings.note: In parallel the array's operating voltage is always below the 33 V Voc, so a 20 A input cannot take 660 W. The true ceiling is lower and depends on the panel's Vmp, which I could not read. Rated-output arithmetic; real output is lower.

findings.label: Voc, Isc, connector
findings.note: $399 each (storecheck, 2026-11-18). The page FAQ advises against mixing panel types (PV200 with SP200L).

findings.label: Two 200 W panels against the 60 V / 20 A input (arithmetic)
findings.value: Series: 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V Voc, inside 60 V. Parallel: 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A Isc, over 20 A. Series is the fit and passes the full rated 400 W (3,840 / 400 = 9.6 h at rated output)
findings.note: Arithmetic from BLUETTI's SP200L page and the Elite 400 input spec. This assumes the kit's 200 W panels are the SP200L; the kit page does not name the panel model. Kit store price $1,899.00 (storecheck, 2026-11-18).

findings.label: Single 350 W panel against the input
findings.value: 33 V Voc sits inside the 12–60 V window; one panel, one included MC4-to-XT60 cable
